description: Analysis of modern x86-64 hardware capabilities and microarchitectural opportunities for DEFLATE decompression optimization.

BMI1.relevance: TZCNT and LZCNT useful for counting bits in decode operations. ANDN eliminates NOT+AND sequences.

BMI2.relevance: Critical for Huffman decode. BZHI extracts variable-width bitfields in 1 cycle. SHRX/SHLX avoid register pressure from cl-dependent shifts. PDEP/PEXT for bit manipulation.
BMI2.caveat: PDEP/PEXT are SLOW on AMD pre-Zen 3 (>15 cycles microcode-emulated vs 1 cycle on Intel). Must have fallback paths.

AVX2.relevance: 256-bit copies for match/literal operations. VPGATHERDD can do 8 parallel table lookups but has high latency (~12 cycles on Skylake, ~21 on Zen 2). VPSHUFB for byte shuffling in overlapping match copies.

AVX-512.availability: Skylake-X (Intel 2017), Zen 4 (AMD 2022). Disabled on Alder Lake E-cores.
AVX-512.relevance: 512-bit copies, VPCOMPRESSD for conditional stores. Downclocking risk on some Intel SKUs reduces attractiveness. Zen 4 implements via 256-bit double-pump.
AVX-512.recommendation: Use only for copy operations; avoid in hot decode loop due to frequency throttling risk.

VPCLMULQDQ.relevance: Primarily for CRC32/Adler32 checksums, not Huffman decode. Can accelerate hash functions.

instruction_latency_throughput.description: Key instruction timings for Huffman decode hot loop on modern microarchitectures

huffman_decode_branches.name: subtable_redirect
huffman_decode_branches.impact: Minor: longer codes are rare with 11+ bit primary table

huffman_decode_branches.name: match_copy_overlap_check
huffman_decode_branches.impact: Moderate: distance < length is common for repetitive data

branch_misprediction_analysis.strategy: Eliminate branches in the hot loop. Use branchless refill, conditional moves (CMOV) for dispatch where possible, and separate fast paths for literals (which are predictable). The literal/match dispatch is the hardest branch to eliminate because the two paths have very different behavior.

decode_table_footprint.fits_in_l1: Yes, comfortably. Even with 32KB output window, total working set is ~50 KB.

output_window.fits_in_l1: Barely (32KB L1 on Zen, 48KB on Golden Cove). Recent match copies hit L1; distant copies may miss.
output_window.prefetch_strategy: Not needed for typical access patterns. Sequential output writes are hardware-prefetched. Match copies within recent history (distance < 4KB) are reliably in L1.

input_stream.access_pattern: Sequential reads, highly predictable. Hardware prefetcher handles this well.
input_stream.prefetch_strategy: No explicit prefetch needed. The branchless refill loads 8 bytes per refill, overlapping naturally with decode.

cache_and_prefetch_considerations.cache_line_alignment: Decode tables should be 64-byte aligned for optimal cache line utilization. Match copies should use aligned stores when possible (but unaligned is fast on modern x86).

BZHI_for_bit_extraction.use_case: Extract variable-width bitfield from the bit buffer. After a table lookup returns the code length (N bits), BZHI extracts the low N bits of the next codeword in a single cycle.
BZHI_for_bit_extraction.example:
// Extract extra bits for length code
extra_bits = _bzhi_u64(saved_bitbuf >> code_len, extra_bit_count);
BZHI_for_bit_extraction.benefit: Replaces a shift + mask sequence (2 instructions, 2 cycles) with 1 instruction (1 cycle). In the hot loop executing billions of times, this saves ~10% of decode cycles.

PDEP_for_bit_scatter.use_case: Deposit bits from a compact source into scattered positions defined by a mask. Could be used to construct multi-symbol table entries during table build phase.
PDEP_for_bit_scatter.example:
// Pack (symbol, code_len, extra_bits) into a 32-bit table entry
entry = _pdep_u64(symbol, 0xFF0000) | _pdep_u64(code_len, 0xF) | _pdep_u64(extra_count, 0xF00);
PDEP_for_bit_scatter.benefit: Simplifies table entry construction. Not useful in the decode hot loop.
PDEP_for_bit_scatter.caveat: SLOW on AMD pre-Zen3 (>15 cycles). Use only in table build phase where it's called once per block.

TZCNT_for_zero_detection.use_case: Count trailing zeros to find the next set bit. Useful for detecting stored block boundaries (which are byte-aligned) or finding sync points in the bitstream.
TZCNT_for_zero_detection.example:
// Find next potential block header (byte-aligned position with BTYPE bits)
zeros = _tzcnt_u64(candidate_mask);
TZCNT_for_zero_detection.benefit: Single-cycle bit scanning replaces a loop. Useful for block-boundary detection in parallel decode strategies.
TZCNT_for_zero_detection.performance: 1 cycle latency on both Intel and AMD modern cores.

SHRX_SHLX_for_shift_without_cl.instruction: SHRX r64, r64, r64 / SHLX r64, r64, r64
SHRX_SHLX_for_shift_without_cl.use_case: Variable shift where the shift amount is in any register (not just cl). Critical in the decode hot loop where the shift amount comes from a table lookup, freeing cl for other uses.
SHRX_SHLX_for_shift_without_cl.example:
// Consume bits: shift bit buffer right by code_length
bitbuf = _shrx_u64(bitbuf, code_length_reg);
SHRX_SHLX_for_shift_without_cl.benefit: Eliminates MOV to cl + SHR sequence (saves 1 instruction, 1 cycle, and reduces register pressure). ISA-L's assembly uses this extensively.
SHRX_SHLX_for_shift_without_cl.fallback: On non-BMI2: mov cl, code_length; shr rax, cl
